For this node, the investable bottleneck appears to split into at least four public-market layers: reference electrical-equipment leaders, niche switchgear/packaged-power suppliers, electrical infrastructure contractors, and small component suppliers for T&D/substations.

Need a follow-up search focused specifically on US-listed transformer, bushing, transformer-oil, grain-oriented electrical steel, relay/protection, and cable suppliers; this pass found stronger public evidence for switchgear and electrical construction than for pure transformer components.

POWL should be tracked as a direct switchgear/electrical-distribution bottleneck candidate for AI data-center power infrastructure; evidence strength is higher because management disclosed data-center orders and record backlog.

AMSC is a newly relevant transformer/grid-resiliency candidate after acquiring Comtrafo; keep as underfollowed but require verification of U.S. data-center applicability, voltage class, certifications, and customer mix.
MYRG is a services-side chokepoint candidate where the scarce asset may be electrical construction labor, substation capability, and T&D execution rather than proprietary equipment.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion for the grid-interconnection power-equipment node. The reference lane is represented by Eaton as the obvious large-cap electrical-equipment leader with direct data-center order momentum and switchgear capacity additions. The underfollowed lane prioritizes public companies closer to project execution, engineered electrical systems, and site/electrical infrastructure: Powell Industries, IES Holdings, and Sterling Infrastructure. These are not recommendations; they are research candidates for later evidence, valuation, customer-concentration, backlog-quality, and margin-sustainability checks. Layer 1B expansion for the power-infrastructure chokepoint finds one reference leader and three less-obvious US-listed suppliers/contractors tied to switchgear, engineered electrical infrastructure, transmission/substation construction, and grid-line hardware. The strongest directly evidenced underfollowed name in this pass is Powell Industries, where recent company disclosures tie backlog and orders to data-center power systems. IES Holdings and MYR Group are plausible second-order beneficiaries via data-center electrical infrastructure and grid/substation construction. Preformed Line Products is a lower-confidence component/hardware hypothesis for transmission and substation buildout rather than direct AI data-center exposure.
